title: Illinois, California governors fast-track AI safety measures with EOs
content:
Illinois, California governors fast-track AI safety measures with executive orders
Sept. 22, 2026 — Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker and California Gov. Gavin Newsom both took executive action over the past four days to address the dangers of unchecked AI models.
Responding to concerns arising from recent AI incidents involving frontier models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic, Illinois Gov. Pritzker this morning issued an executive order to create the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet. The AI Cabinet will marshal the knowledge of experts in the AI field and key leaders in state government, “to ensure that the progress of AI is appropriately regulated and monitored.”
Pritzker’s EO followed California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s AI policy executive order issued on Friday. That action will accelerate California’s new law establishing first-in-the-nation independent oversight of AI companies, and advance the creation of an “AI kill switch.”
The details: Illinois Executive order on AI
The new Illinois AI Cabinet will advise state government on preparing for and responding to AI-related incidents, identifying safeguards for public assets and infrastructure, and evaluating additional steps government officials can take to strengthen AI safety and accountability.
Gov. Pritzker will seek input from state agency leaders and announce members of the cabinet in the coming weeks. The AI cabinet will include a broad cross-sector of experts from academia, law, ethics, and governance.
Senior state agency leaders include executives from the Dept. of Innovation and Technology, the Emergency Management Agency, the Dept. of Financial and Professional Regulation, the Commerce Commission, the State Police, the Dept. of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, the Environmental Protection Agency, and the Dept. of Public Health.
Building on the 2026 AI Safety Measures Act
Gov. Pritzker’s executive order builds on the foundation of the Illinois AI Safety Measures Act of 2026. That law, authored by Sen. Mary Edly-Allen and supported by the Transparency Coalition, established a requirement for independent third-party AI safety audits.
“Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said. “Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority.  Congress and the White House need to treat AI risks with urgency, but in the meantime, Illinois won’t wait because it is our foremost responsibility to prepare and protect Illinoisians.”

The details: California Executive Order on AI
Gov. Newsom’s executive order convenes a group of world-leading experts to provide, within two months, a guide for California to reinforce and strengthen its AI safety and security laws.
Proposals under consideration include requiring independent third parties to write safety plans for frontier AI companies, as well as requiring companies to develop an emergency shutoff for frontier models.
Accelerate IVO regs: Newsom’s EO moves up the timeline for the creation of state requirements for IVOs, independent verification organizations that are expected to act as third-party verification firms to ensure that safety measures are implemented and state AI laws are followed. The recently signed bill, SB 813, authorizing those actions called for a deadline of Jan. 1, 2028. The EO moves that up to May 1, 2027.
As in Illinois, Gov. Newsom’s EO builds on new 2026 state laws requiring independent third-party safety audits for frontier AI models. SB 813, authored by Sen. Jerry McNerney (D-Pleasanton), establishes a first-in-the-nation framework for independent verification organizations (IVOs) that can assess AI systems and models for compliance with state law. AB 1405, authored by Assm. Rebecca Bauer-Kahan (D-Orinda), creates a state registry for AI auditors and establishing standards for their independence, transparency, and integrity.
Fast-turn recommendations: The EO also tasks the state Government Operations Agency and the Governor’s Office of Emergency Services to create, within the next eight weeks, a list of potential amendments to existing state laws that would improve AI safety.
Those recommendations should focus on these four areas:
- Requirements that all large frontier developers embed designated IVOs onsite in their labs to conduct periodic audits and evaluations.
- Requirements that the safety frameworks, transparency reports, and risk assessments that frontier AI companies are required to file be independently verified.
- Requirements around the creation of a “kill switch” for frontier models, with the efficacy of the switch verified on an ongoing basis by an IVO.
- Updating the definition of critical safety incidents that AI companies are required to report to include a range of loss-of-control incidents, covering recently reported incidents from large frontier developers.

report.summary: Illinois and California governors issued executive orders to speed AI safety oversight, audits, and frontier-model controls.
report.background: The executive actions follow recent AI incidents involving frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic, which intensified concerns about unchecked AI risks. With federal legislation stalled, states are filling the gap. Illinois builds on its 2026 AI Safety Measures Act requiring independent third-party safety audits. California builds on SB 813 and AB 1405, which created a first-in-the-nation framework for independent verification organizations and a state registry for AI auditors. Both governors are using executive orders to accelerate timelines, convene experts, and propose stronger safeguards, including emergency shutoff mechanisms, independent verification, and expanded incident reporting for frontier AI developers.
key_points: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker created the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet by executive order. The cabinet will advise state government on AI incident response, safeguard public assets and infrastructure, and evaluate additional AI safety and accountability measures. It will include experts from academia, law, ethics, governance, and senior state agency leaders.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order to accelerate the state's AI oversight law and advance an 'AI kill switch.' It convenes experts to recommend safety and security rules within two months, including independent third-party safety plans and emergency shutoff requirements for frontier models.

Newsom's order moves up the deadline for independent verification organization regulations from Jan. 1, 2028, to May 1, 2027. IVOs would act as third-party firms verifying that AI companies implement safety measures and comply with state law, building on SB 813 and AB 1405.

California's Government Operations Agency and Office of Emergency Services must propose legal amendments within eight weeks. Focus areas include onsite IVO audits, independent verification of safety frameworks and transparency reports, verified kill switches, and broader reporting of loss-of-control incidents.

Both states are acting after recent frontier-model incidents and amid federal inaction. Pritzker urged Congress and the White House to treat AI risks urgently, but said Illinois will not wait, reflecting a growing state-led push for AI safety and accountability.
report.impact: For the AI industry, these orders signal rising compliance obligations: frontier developers may face mandated third-party audits, onsite IVO reviewers, verified kill switches, and expanded incident reporting. That could create a new market for audit and verification firms, but also a patchwork of state rules. Developers should prepare for stricter documentation, risk assessments, and transparency requirements. Regular users may benefit from more reliable safety checks and clearer accountability, though compliance costs could slow some deployments or favor larger labs. The bigger signal is that states are willing to regulate frontier AI directly while federal policy remains unsettled.
report.tools: To follow the audit and oversight trend, watch UK AI Safety Institute's Inspect framework, METR evaluations, MLCommons AI Safety benchmarks, NIST AI RMF, and Stanford HELM. Open-source projects such as AI Verify, OpenMined, and Model Cards help teams document risks and evidence. These are not state IVOs, but they show how third-party verification, red-teaming, and incident reporting may be operationalized.
